effects: Exactly `assets` USDC moves from the signer to the vault (safeTransferFrom in enter), using an approval the signer already gave.
New CSBUSDC vault shares are minted to `onBehalf`. The number is previewDeposit(assets), worked out from the vault's stored share price after interest is accrued.
No native value is taken (not payable). The vault may move the deposit on to its liquidity adapter, but that is the vault's own money, not the signer's.
formats.shown: Deposit an exact USDC amount into the Clearstar CSBUSDC vault, with the shares sent to the named onBehalf address.

findings.title: deposit: the number of CSBUSDC shares minted is not shown; it comes from the stored share price.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol deposit(): `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets);` comes after accrueInterest(). The calldata has only assets and onBehalf. The screen shows 'Deposit asset' and a constant 'Share ticker', with no share amount.
findings.fix: None possible in calldata. The share amount is derived on chain.

cases.notes: The signer sent exactly 1 USDC, as shown. The 1e18 CSBUSDC shares went to 0xdEaD (signer null), and the screen says so in 'Send shares to'.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: CSBUSDC shares are burned from `onBehalf`. The number is previewWithdraw(assets), rounded up from the stored share price.
If the signer is not `onBehalf`, the owner's share allowance to the signer goes down by that number of shares.
Exactly `assets` USDC goes from the vault to `receiver`.
formats.shown: Withdraw an exact USDC amount to the receiver, taken from the shares of the named Owner.

findings.title: withdraw: the number of CSBUSDC shares burned from the owner is not shown; it comes from the stored share price.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol withdraw(): `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets); exit(...)` then `deleteShares(onBehalf, shares)`. Case 1: 4894407793142420 CSBUSDC went out from the signer, and the screen shows only 'Withdraw exactly 0.0049 USDC' and 'Owner'.
findings.fix: None possible in calldata. A label like 'Owner (shares burned)' could make it clear the shares come from that address.

findings.title: withdraw: neither the intent nor any field names the CSBUSDC share token being burned.
findings.evidence: interpolatedIntent 'Withdraw {#.assets} to {#.receiver}' has no field for $.metadata.constants.vaultTicker, while deposit has a 'Share ticker' field. The case 1 reader wrote 'the screen doesn't name them'.
findings.fix: Add a constant field such as 'Shares burned from: CSBUSDC' using $.metadata.constants.vaultTicker, as deposit does.

cases.notes: The USDC coming in (0.0049, to the signer) matches the screen exactly. The 4894407793142420 CSBUSDC going out is not on screen as an amount or a token; only 'Owner' implies the signer's shares are used.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: If the signer is not `onBehalf`, the owner's share allowance to the signer goes down by `shares`.
USDC worth previewRedeem(shares), worked out from the stored share price with no minimum bound, goes from the vault to `receiver`.
formats.shown: Redeem an exact number of CSBUSDC shares, with the proceeds sent to the receiver, from the named Owner.

findings.title: redeem: the asset received (USDC) is not named anywhere on the screen.
findings.evidence: The descriptor redeem fields are only shares (tokenPath @.to), receiver and onBehalf. VaultV2.sol exit(): `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets)`. In case 2, 501062.190870 USDC came in, and the reader had to assume USDC.
findings.fix: Add a constant field, e.g. label 'Receive asset' with value $.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker, or put 'for USDC' in the interpolatedIntent.

findings.title: redeem: the USDC amount received is decided by the share price, and the call has no minimum-out.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol redeem(): `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares);`. There is no min-assets parameter. Case 2: 501062190870 USDC came in, not shown on screen.

cases.notes: The 499960.495331160640468254 CSBUSDC going out is shown exactly. The 501062.19 USDC coming in has no amount and no asset name; the reader guessed USDC.
